# Introduction

**Sequence-Space Synaesthesia (SSS)**, is the phenomenon where people visualize ordered sequences in consistent spatial positions [@galton1880; @flournoy1893]. **Consistency tasks** classify SSS from controls by having participants indicate perceived spatial positions for a stimuli on a screen. Because of SSS internal spatial representations responses are more consistent than those of controls. Existing **consistency methods** [i.e. @rothen2016] test the spatial variability to the same stimuli, here we explored novel consistency methods.

# Methods

**Consistency tasks** measure the responses (as a *x,y* screen position) for weekdays (Mon-Sun), months (Jan-Dec) and numbers (1-9), each repeated three times. The novel **consistency methods** *B)* and *D)* evaluate participant's *space-form* consistency (Figure 1).

## Aggregated datasets of consistency tasks

We aggregated four available datasets using the same consistency task [@rothen2016; @vanpetersen2020; @ward2022a] and Ward (2025, personal communication). Original groups are defined by self-report of having SSS or not (i.e. controls).

# Results

Receiver Operator Curves (ROC) of each consistency methods show the sensitivity (SSS classified as SSS) and sensibility (control as controls) by moving threshold for each consistency method.

```{r, defineDPfun}
DP <- function(sensitivity, specificity){
  sensitivity = sensitivity/100
  specificity = specificity/100
  return(sqrt(3/pi)*(log(sensitivity/(1-sensitivity)) + log(specificity/(1-specificity))))
}
```

```{r InitializeROC_fun}
## Define function to compute ROC:
Comp_ROC <- function(data, group_col, feature, ID, Ord){
  # Ord: must be: moreSyn or moreCtl. Wheter feature value is moer in Syn or ctl.
  if(!setequal(levels(data[[group_col]]), c("Syn","Ctl"))){
    return(warning("group name must inculde: Syn Ctl"))
    break
  }
  
  if (Ord == "moreSyn") {
    Dirhere <- "<"
  } else if (Ord == "moreCtl") {
    Dirhere <- ">"
  } else {
    return(warning("Ord must be moreSyn or moreCtl"))  
  }
  
  ################ ROC analyses ################ 
  ROC_here <- pROC::roc(data[[group_col]] ~ data[[feature]], data, 
                  direction= Dirhere,
                  percent=TRUE,
                  ci=TRUE, boot.n=100, ci.alpha=0.9, stratified=FALSE,
                  )
  
  # Best threshold using Youden's J
  best_coords <- pROC::coords(ROC_here, "best", 
                              ret = c("accuracy","threshold", "sensitivity","specificity","ppv","npv"), 
                              best.method = "youden")
  

  auc_val <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(ROC_here))
  ci_auc  <- ci.auc(ROC_here)
  ciobj   <- pROC::ci.se(ROC_here, # CI of sensitivity
               specificities=seq(0, 100, 5)) # over a select set of specificities

  new_row <- data.frame(
    Feature   = feature,
    AUC        = round(auc_val, 4),
    DP         = DP(as.numeric(best_coords[["sensitivity"]]),as.numeric(best_coords[["specificity"]])),
    threshold  = as.numeric(best_coords[["threshold"]]),
    sensitivity= as.numeric(best_coords[["sensitivity"]]),
    specificity= as.numeric(best_coords[["specificity"]]),
    accuracy =as.numeric(best_coords[["accuracy"]]),
    # ci_low     = as.numeric(ci_auc[1]),
    # ci_high    = as.numeric(ci_auc[3]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  ################ Contingency table ################ 
    if (Ord == "moreSyn") {
    data$diagnosis <- ifelse(data[[feature]] >= best_coords$threshold,  "Test : Syn", "Test : Ctl")
  } else if (Ord == "moreCtl") {
    data$diagnosis <- ifelse(data[[feature]] >= best_coords$threshold,  "Test : Ctl","Test : Syn")
  } else {
    warning("Ord must be moreSyn or moreCtl")  
  }
  
  tab_counts <- table(data[[group_col]], data$diagnosis)
  
  tab_percent <- prop.table(tab_counts, margin = 1) * 100
  
  result <- matrix(
    paste0(tab_counts, " (", round(tab_percent, 1), "%)"),
    nrow = nrow(tab_counts),
    dimnames = dimnames(tab_counts)
  )
  
  ################ General description ################ 
  # Attention, na removed  
  Descr_table <- data %>%
    group_by(!!sym(group_col)) %>%
    summarize(n = length(unique(!!sym(ID))), Mean = mean(!!sym(feature), na.rm = TRUE), SD = sd(!!sym(feature), na.rm = TRUE))

  ################ Return outputs ################ 
  return(list(ROC_properties = new_row, Coningency_table =result, Descr_table = Descr_table, ROC_curve = ROC_here, CI = ciobj))
}
```

```{r AUCtest, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Multiple comparison issue (need ot adjust p val):
# AUC_test  <- roc.test(ds_Q$group, ds_Q$isValid_perm_M, ds_Q$Perimeter_zs,  boot.n=1000, method = "bootstrap")
# AUC_test2 <- roc.test(ds_Q$group, ds_Q$Perimeter_zs, ds_Q$isValidStruct_M,  boot.n=1000, method = "bootstrap")
# AUC_test3 <- roc.test(ds_Q$group, ds_Q$isValid_perm_M, ds_Q$isValidStruct_M,  boot.n=1000, method = "bootstrap")

# Compare ALL the features and adjust, but leads to the same results.
nFeat    <- length(ROC_curves)
Odd_idx  <- seq(1,nFeat,by=2)
Pair_idx <- seq(2,nFeat,by=2)

ROC_listed <- list()
Feattype <- c()
for(i in 1:nFeat){
  ROC_listed[[i]] <- ROC_curves[[Odd_idx[i]]]
  Feattype <- c(Feattype,ROC_curves[[Pair_idx[i]]])
}

allAUC  <- sapply(ROC_listed, auc)
sel_auc <- which(allAUC == sort(allAUC, decreasing = TRUE)[1])
toCompare_roc <- ROC_listed[[sel_auc]] 

statistic <- sapply(seq_along(ROC_listed), function(i) {
  if (i == sel_auc) return(NA)
  roc.test(toCompare_roc, ROC_listed[[i]],  boot.n=1000,method = "bootstrap")$statistic
})

pvals <- sapply(seq_along(ROC_listed), function(i) {
  if (i == sel_auc) return(NA)
  roc.test(toCompare_roc, ROC_listed[[i]],  boot.n=1000,method = "bootstrap")$p.value
})

# Adjust for multiple comparison: the order is Feattype
pvals_adj <- p.adjust(pvals, method = "fdr") # or fdr since exploratory, lead to the same.

Results_ROCcomp <- data.frame(
  Feature = Feattype,
  D = statistic, 
  pvals = pvals_adj,
  isSign = (pvals_adj <.05)
)

save(Results_ROCcomp,"Results_ROCcomp.Rdata")
```

**Permuted validity** and **standardized perimeter** led to comparably high AUC (*D* = `r round(Results_ROCcomp[Results_ROCcomp$Feature == "Perimeter_zs",]$D,2)`, *n.s.*). **Polsby-Popper**, differed from permuted validity (*D* = `r round(Results_ROCcomp[Results_ROCcomp$Feature == "pp_M",]$D,2)`, *p* \< .05).

However some results varied depending on the datasets:

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=6}
gp_Sensitivity <- ggplot(AUC_ds, aes(x = dataSource, y = Sensitivity, group = Feature, colour = Feature)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_manual(values =Colors_here) + 
  papaja::theme_apa() +
  xlab(' ') +
  ylim(20,100) +
  theme(legend.position="none",axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, vjust = 0.8, hjust = 0.6, size = 8))

gp_Specificity <- ggplot(AUC_ds, aes(x = dataSource, y = Specificity, group = Feature, colour = Feature)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_color_manual(values =Colors_here) + 
  papaja::theme_apa() +
  xlab(' ') +
  ylim(20,100) +
  theme(legend.position="none", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, vjust = 0.8, hjust = 0.6, size = 8))


legend <- get_legend(
  ggplot(AUC_ds, aes(x = dataSource, y = Specificity, group = Feature, colour = Feature)) +
    geom_point() +
    papaja::theme_apa() +
    scale_color_manual(values =Colors_here) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
    theme(legend.justification = c(0.22,0.1), legend.position = "bottom",
           legend.text=ggplot2::element_text(size=8))
)

plot_grid(gp_AUC, gp_DP,gp_Sensitivity,gp_Specificity, 
          labels = c("A","B","D","E"),
          legend = legend, ncol=2,
          rel_heights = c(1, 1.4, 0.21)) # height of each row. 3rd row is legend, 10% of the others. # height of each row. 3rd row is legend, 10% of the others.

```

# Discussion

- `r colorize::colorize("Permuted validity","#b2df8a")` underlines the possible role of topological rules for SSS space-forms, with the `r round(All_ROC[All_ROC$Feature == "isValid_perm_M",]$threshold,2)` cut-off reflecting an average of `r round(All_ROC[All_ROC$Feature == "isValid_perm_M",]$threshold,2)*9` valid forms out of 9.

- `r colorize::colorize("Polsby-popper","#CAB2D6")` score [@polsby1991], originally designed to measure district compactness, performs surprisingly well in distinguishing SSS from controls, tough it's low sensitivity.

- `r colorize::colorize("Perimeter","#6A33C2")` captures spatial variability within stimuli.

Earlier methods [@rothen2016] allowed controls to achieve artificially high consistency by clicking on the same position. While this limitation is adressed by novel methods. However, these interoduces a new issue: reduced detection of zig-zag SSS space-forms. Moreover, both methods lead to comparable classification performances. Overall, we find some heterogeneities in classification performances across datasets, motivating additional further valiadation in *Phase II* on yet-to-be collected data.

In sum, `r colorize::colorize("validity","#b2df8a")` is as effective as previous methods for classifying SSS. Nevertheless, these results suggests the space-forms of SSS might be mapped following topographical rules such as for cartography.
